_comment: Reviewed BTXRD near-duplicate candidates (runs/btxrd-near-duplicates-20261024T071231Z, ranks 22-37 and 42, the top 16 new pairs plus one more benign/normal pair). Only 'same_image' pairs are merged into a duplicate_group by build_manifest. Same-patient views are not grouped: that would be inferred patient grouping, which Hub D04 rules out. Reviewed 2026-10-24 by Claude Code for Sebastian, by side-by-side inspection and pixel comparison; pending a second human look.

same_image.evidence: Identical 2360x1250 size, full-frame pixel correlation 0.997 at 256 px width; the only visible difference is a text label burned into IMG002677. Embedding cosine: RAD-DINO 1.0, ResNet-50 0.9924. Both normal. Crossed the image-stratified split before this record.

pending.reason: Same hip and pose by eye; 552 vs 535 px wide at equal height. Best crop alignment corr 0.957, best rescale 0.971: either one radiograph processed twice or two exposures moments apart. Needs a person. Both malignant.

separate_exposures.note: Different positioning, marker placement or side: separate radiographs, likely of one patient. Not grouped (no inferred patients).

label_notes: IMG000626 (benign) / IMG002623 (normal) are a left and a right knee; IMG000384 (benign) / IMG002854 (normal) and IMG000495 (benign) / IMG001923 (normal) are different exposures. These labels need not conflict, but they show near-identical images can carry different labels.
